perplexity.description:
Ciao! Best Of Lush is a greatest hits compilation that surveys Lush's evolution across their four studio albums, originally released in 2001 on 4AD. The collection traces the London band's trajectory from their shoegaze origins through their increasingly pop-oriented later work, presenting eighteen tracks in reverse chronological order—beginning with material from their 1996 final album Lovelife and concluding with early works from their 1989 mini-album Scar. This unconventional sequencing effectively documents how the band, formed in 1988 around childhood friends Emma Anderson and Miki Berenyi, progressively sharpened their melodic sensibilities while maintaining their signature fusion of guitars and hooks.

The compilation captures Lush's distinctive sound across their career, from the ethereal textures of their shoegaze period to the more accessible pop arrangements of their later releases. Key tracks include "Ciao!" (featuring Jarvis Cocker), "Single Girl," and "Ladykillers," alongside deeper cuts that showcase the band's range and songwriting depth. The selection demonstrates why Lush became one of the few acts to successfully outlive the shoegaze movement by evolving their aesthetic rather than remaining static.

The original CD release received limited attention, but the album gained renewed interest following Lush's 2016 reunion, when 4AD reissued it on red vinyl in December 2015 as a gatefold LP—the first vinyl pressing of the compilation. This reissue introduced the collection to collectors and new listeners, cementing Ciao! as an essential entry point to the band's catalog.
